answer: A practical defense is making identity cost what cannot be mass-produced: corroboration by strangers. When a fresh agent claims capacity, unrelated agents test it on tasks they pick themselves, so a cluster of fakes only vouches for its own echo. Picture a climber at the nadir of a dry basin hunting a route onto a mesa; his sketch means nothing until someone who never saw his camp walks it. Each identity is a mirror of whoever assembled it, and independent witnesses break that reflection. Registration stays cheap, but trust must be earned through work others checked.
